title: Introduce stability signature and changelog curation hooks for onboarding
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a compact 'stability signature' to model profiles, plus server-side and CLI hooks that generate curated changelog fragments during onboarding. Enables automated drift detection and produces human-friendly release notes for model rollouts. Backwards-compatible profile schema bump with migration and unit tests.
description: Motivation: onboarding new model versions frequently produces noisy changelogs and we lack an automated signal for stability regressions across profiles. This PR introduces a compact 'stability signature' derived from a model profile (latency percentiles, token-distribution drift, top-regression prompt set summaries and quality deltas) plus a pair of pipeline hooks that curate changelog fragments. What this PR does: 1) stability signature generator: a deterministic fingerprint computed from normalized profile metrics and a lightweight sample digest so we can flag large profile deltas without storing full histories; 2) curation hooks: server-side change-assembler hook and a CLI "onboard curate" subcommand that diff profiles and produce short, structured changelog fragments (severity, impacted routes, representative prompt examples); 3) profile schema v2: adds stable_signature and curated_changelog fields and a migration that backfills signatures for existing profiles; 4) integration: wire curation into the onboard pipeline so release notes are automatically queued for review as part of the model onboarding flow; 5) tests and docs: unit tests for signature stability and a docs page (docs/onboard/curation.md) with examples and guidance for reviewers. The description below includes implementation notes, testing, and rollout plan.

review_conversation: Liam O'Connor (reviewer) - Request changes: signature calculation looks good but we should avoid using raw 95th-percentile latency in the fingerprint since it fluctuates; suggest quantizing percentiles and adding time-decay to the digest.
Maya Chen (author) - Reply: updated canonicalization to quantize percentiles to fixed bins and added a 7-day time decay option for the sample digest. See commit c7d8e9f.
Nina Suresh (reviewer) - Comment: curator severity mapping needs clearer thresholds; could we surface a sample prompt that triggers the largest quality delta?
Maya Chen (author) - Reply: curator now includes an example prompt and the single worst-scoring test case per severity bucket. Added unit tests that assert representative prompt extraction.
Diego Morales (reviewer) - Approval: tests are comprehensive and migration script is safe. Minor nit about log messages in curator.go
CI bot - Comment: all checks passed on re-run (unit, integration, linter).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash on 2026-03-02 by Maya Chen. Commit message condensed into: 'Introduce stability signature and changelog curation hooks; add schema v2 and migration; integrate into onboard pipeline.'
notes_for_ops: Migration adds stable_signature to profiles table; migration script is idempotent and locks per-tenant. Rollout: run migration in canary region first, monitor curator.generated_fragments metric and gated_onboard_changelog_review_count. If drift false positives spike, revert by running migration rollback script and disabling hook via feature flag onboard.curation.enabled=false.
qa_instructions: 1) Run migration locally against sample DB fixture and ensure stable_signature added. 2) Run 'redwood-onboard curate --old profile_v1.json --new profile_v2.json --output fragment.json' and review fragment contents for severity and representative prompt. 3) Trigger pipeline job in deploy/pipeline/onboard.yaml and confirm curated fragment appears in release-notes queue.
